correctness.rationale: For weighted Dirichlet monomials e_k=(k+1)^((alpha-1)/2)z^k, D_{t,theta}^{(m)} maps e_{j+m} into scalar e_j, with scalar (j+m)!/j! e^(-tj)((j+1)/(j+m+1))^((1-alpha)/2)e^(ijtheta). The difference has mutually orthogonal columns and exact singular values with factor |1-e^(ijtheta)|. Since amplitude=j^m(1+O(1/j)), t^(mp+1) sum is uniformly reducible to t sum h(tj)g(jtheta), including 0<p<1, by exponential tails. Rational angle θ=2πa/q+ωt+o(t) gives q residue-class Riemann integrals; irrational fixed limits and super-t detuning follow from Fourier polynomial approximation and the geometric/Abel bound O(t/|1-e^(ikθ)|). Beta integration supplies the Haar factor. For m=1,p=4,q=2 the average phase polynomial is 6+2cos(2ωx), so the gamma Laplace integral gives F(ω)=Γ(5)[6/4^5+2Re(4-2iω)^(-5)] and a strict rational detuning dip. Checked the finite diagnostic script's assumptions; no finite samples establish all-angle claims.
